subject: Civil Engineering
title: Traffic Signals and Timing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Traffic Signals and Timing usable.

hook.text: A red light isn't random. Every second of green, yellow, and red is calculated.

buildup.text: Cycle length is the total time for all signal phases. Longer cycles handle more traffic.

discovery.text: Webster's formula calculates the optimal cycle length to minimize total delay.

twist.text: Coordinated signals create a 'green wave' — hit one green and you hit them all.

climax.text: Adaptive signals use real-time sensors to adjust timing on the fly — AI-powered traffic.

punchline.text: A well-timed light moves thousands of cars without anyone noticing.

quiz.question: What does Webster's formula optimize in traffic signal design?
options: The number of traffic signals needed per intersection
The cycle length to minimize total vehicle delay
The brightness of signal lights for driver visibility

details.summary: Traffic signals control vehicle and pedestrian movements at intersections using timed phases that assign right-of-way to competing traffic streams. Signal timing optimization balances green time among approaches to minimize total delay while ensuring safe clearance intervals between conflicting.
details.whyItMatters: Optimized signal timing can increase intersection capacity by 20-30% without any physical construction. Poor timing wastes fuel, increases emissions, and frustrates millions of commuters daily.
takeaways: Signal cycle length typically ranges from 60 to 120 seconds
Green time is allocated based on traffic volume on each approach
Coordination between adjacent signals creates green waves for progression

faq.question: How do actuated traffic signals differ from fixed-time signals?
faq.answer: Fixed-time signals cycle through the same pattern regardless of traffic. Actuated signals use detectors embedded in the pavement or cameras to sense vehicle presence and adjust green times in real time, reducing delay during low-volume periods.

faq.question: What is a green wave in traffic signal coordination?
faq.answer: A green wave offsets signal timing along a corridor so that vehicles traveling at a target speed encounter successive green lights without stopping. This requires careful calculation of distances between signals and consistent cycle lengths.
